user_journeys.description: General website navigation and content discovery

proposed_scenarios.scenario_name: Verify Successful Homepage Load and Core UI Elements - Smoke Test
proposed_scenarios.description: This fundamental smoke test scenario verifies that the Docker Hub homepage is accessible and loads correctly. It ensures that critical, above-the-fold UI components, such as the main navigation, search bar, and sign-in options, are present and visible. Successfully passing this test provides confidence that the site is online and the basic application shell has rendered, which is a prerequisite for any further user interaction testing.
proposed_scenarios.business_goal: Validate that the primary entry point of the Docker Hub service is online, accessible, and renders the essential UI for user interaction.
proposed_scenarios.user_story: As a new user, I want to load the Docker Hub homepage, so that I can see the main features and begin searching for container images.

detailed_steps.action: Navigate to the Docker Hub homepage
detailed_steps.description: Initiate the test by navigating the browser directly to the Docker Hub homepage at https://hub.docker.com/. This step establishes the starting point for the test. The browser should successfully resolve the URL and begin loading the page assets. Wait for the page to reach a stable, fully loaded state before proceeding with any verifications. This means all initial HTML, CSS, and JavaScript have been processed, and the main page structure is rendered in the DOM.

selector_reference.selection_reason: This is a 'navigate' action which does not require an element selector. The action is performed using a direct browser navigation command like page.goto().

detailed_steps.wait_strategy: Wait for the page's 'load' event to fire and for network activity to become idle. This ensures all synchronous resources are loaded. Allow a total timeout of up to 15 seconds to account for network variability. The primary indicator of success is the browser tab showing the correct page title and favicon.
detailed_steps.verification_strategy: Confirm the browser's current URL is exactly 'https://hub.docker.com/'. Verify that the page title contains the text 'Docker Hub'. Check the HTTP response status code to ensure it is 200 OK. This confirms that the navigation was successful and the server responded correctly without redirects or errors.
detailed_steps.error_recovery: If the page fails to load within the 15-second timeout, perform one retry after a 3-second delay. If the retry also fails, capture a screenshot, log any console errors, and fail the test with a clear message indicating a 'Homepage Navigation Failure', including the target URL and the timeout duration.
detailed_steps.business_context: Establishes the initial point of contact for a user with the service. If this fails, no other functionality can be tested or used.

detailed_steps.action: Verify presence of essential homepage elements
detailed_steps.description: After the homepage has successfully loaded, perform a visual check to confirm that key user interface elements are present and visible. This includes locating the main search input field, which is critical for the site's primary function, as well as the 'Sign In' button and the main Docker Hub logo. This verification ensures that the core application framework has rendered correctly and the page is ready for user interaction, not just that the HTML document was served.

selector_reference.selection_reason: No selectors are available in the provided pool. This verification step requires selectors for the search bar, sign-in button, etc., which would need to be manually created during test script implementation as no interaction data was captured.

detailed_steps.wait_strategy: After the initial page load, wait for up to 5 seconds for dynamic elements to become visible. Specifically, wait for an element that is likely to be the search input field (e.g., with placeholder text 'Search Docker Hub') to be visible and enabled before starting verifications.
detailed_steps.verification_strategy: Verify that an input element, likely for search, is visible on the page. Verify that a link or button with the text 'Sign In' is visible. Verify that the Docker logo image is present in the header. The presence of these three elements serves as a strong indicator that the homepage has loaded its critical components successfully.
detailed_steps.error_recovery: If any of the key elements (search input, sign-in button, logo) are not found within a 10-second wait period, capture a screenshot of the current page state. Fail the test with a specific message detailing which element was missing, for example, 'Homepage Verification Failed: Search input field not found'.
detailed_steps.business_context: Confirms that the site is not only online but also functional and ready for users to engage with its core features like search and authentication.

expected_results: The Docker Hub homepage loads successfully within a reasonable time frame.
The browser URL and page title are correct.
Key interactive elements, including the search bar and sign-in button, are visible and rendered correctly.
The test completes without any navigation or element visibility errors.
edge_cases_to_test: Page load behavior on slow network conditions.
Responsiveness of the layout on different viewport sizes (desktop, tablet, mobile).
Handling of ad-blockers or script-blocking browser extensions that might interfere with rendering.
data_requirements: The official URL for the Docker Hub homepage: https://hub.docker.com/
prerequisites: The test environment must have a stable internet connection.
The Docker Hub website (hub.docker.com) must be online and accessible from the test agent's location.
No authentication is required to view the public homepage.
